BGE Ladder Component.
How it works: 
Go to a ladder component and hold the e-key to climb up, down or sideways.
Every ladder component has a property called ladder and the PlayerBox searches for this property
with a near-sensor.
Every time you near to an object that contains the ladder property you get a gameinfo E-Key on the screen so you know that you can climb.
P-Key.................Starts the Game Engine
W-Key.................Move forwards
S-Key.................Move backwards
D-Key.................Move to the right
A-Key.................Move to the left
Hold Spacebar.........Player moves faster
Q-Key.................Jump
F-Key.................Changed the daytime forward
B-Key.................Changed the daytime backward
E-Key.................Climb up

title: T-Splines Rhino School Building 3d model Free 3D print model
formats: 3DM
formats_detail: [{"format": "3DM", "full_name": "Rhinoceros 3D", "file_size": "470 MB", "file_count": 1, "version": "", "renderer": null}]
total_file_size: 3DM:470 MB
description_text:
This building was modeled in Rhino using the T-splines and grasshopper plugins. It was designed for my Masters of Architecture Studio at Pratt Institute in the spring of 2015.
I have 3D printed this model and it comes out nicely on the higher resolution powder printers (Pictures/Renderings below) This model is designed with some hollow splines so as to use less material (cheaper to print) and has void holes in the back of the model in order to get the powder out after printed. It is chopped at the bottom so as to stand upright, and has an elevator core running up the back of the model, also makes the model less fragile. 
This model looks awesome on a desk or on a shelf. This model is already at scale (about 7-8 inches tall), and can be scaled up if you would like. I would not recommend scaling it down as some of the thinner splines can get too small and might break when excavating the print. 
This model took me around 90 hours to build, you will see the density of the model when you open the file (large file size), but the file still navigates well.  This model can also be imported into Maya, 3DS MAX, Revit, etc. ENJOY!

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Is it a Japanese Tea house? Is it in the Oriental Far East? If you answered yes to either of those questions, I'm sorry to say you are incorrect. But if you said it was in Paulwall then you are indeed correct! Here is a small bungalow house just west of the downtown metro area. It is actually a typical small rectangular bungalow if you think about it. The sharp peaks and long planks were inspired by the Japanese homes made of wood and rice paper. Thank goodness none of this house was made of paper! the porch and chimneys are stuccoed where as the walls are shingle style. Don't stop out here. Come on inside to see striking millwork about the interior. There are built-ins. The dining room also has some fine millwork of its own including a built-in cabinet. You aso get a private porch off the dining room beleive it or not. The kitchen is decked out with retro appliances. in back you get two bedrooms, a bathroom and a sleeping porch, or in other words, a third bedroom if you think about it. Those areas are less intricate. There are a number of other bungalows in the area a lot like this one but minus all the oriental pattern details this one offers. I hope you like this little house and please rate :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 So you are likely already familiar with the fact that Paulwall has a lot of old homes. This one happened to be renovated from its original 4 bedroom, 1 bathroom version to 3 bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms. This is not a Sears Home, though, it is a Gordon Van Tine Home. It is similar to a foursquare house though people may not call it that. Like any kit home, you'd walk into a great big living room, beyond, a dining room, then a kitchen in the far back corner. Basement stairs would be below the main stair. The laundry room used to be the pantry. The furnace is in the basement, then rides a chase up through the house in the form of a chimney. The building itself, built in the 20's is a relic of mail-order homes mass produced for the growth of cities. Sit on its grand porch, the signature item, or in the singanature bay window upstairs. Either way, you might like to live in this home. It is an 8-minute bus ride to downtown Paulwall or in 10 minute walking proximity to the Paulwall College main campus. This is also near a busy shopping center. The house is in a neighborhood full of other beautifully preserved old homes with tree-lined streets. Enjoy and please rate :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Paulwall has an old granite clad city hall. It is known commonly as the community auditorium. Yes, there is a theatre-like auditorium in the rear with a stage, curtains, and skytower. The house has a seating capacity of 500, though the area is currently unaccessable at this time. There is a large seating balcony. though you can't go in, you can see where it exisits on the exterior walls. Paulwall is known well for its ambience in eclectic classical architecture in which you will find in abundance throughout this building. The city lot this building sits on is too small for the complete parking capacity so a seperate lot across the street suffices for it, not modeled here. Half of Paulwall's downtown is just parking lots. Okay, so besides the house in the back, the city offices are in the wings in front. The mayor's office is on the 3rd floor. The smaller building to the right used to be the city library but since they moved, it became offices for the departments of health and education. Ignore the geo-location. Thanks to the contributors for the greenery and google for the flag and dumpsters. everything else was by me. No city is complete without a city hall building. Include in your city backdrop, pefect for downtown. I hope you enjoy one of Paulwall's finest buildings and please rate. IGNORE the geo-location, it isn't real. If you like architecture and want to see more, please check out my community page on Facebook shown by the link given to you below :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a victorian shell from one in BmrCT's collection, thanks to BmrCT. I liked the house so much that I could invision its floor plan even though it was a hollow shell so I gave it a floor plan. What you have are stairs as soon as you walk into the entry. To the left is adining room, to the right is the living room with a window seat. In the back you have the kitchen. The kitchen was designed so you can put a round breakfast table in the center. Off to the side of that is a powder room with a bifold pantry directly next to it. In the far back are the basement stairs and the servant's stairway, you know, like in those old houses. The basement stairs are there, not under the main stairs. That is where the coat closet is. Upstairs there are 3 bedrooms and one bathroom. Up where the gothic window is above the front door is a sitting nook. That's the tour. The cosmetic features have been updated and altered some as you can see when comparing it to the original house. Windows have either been added or removed. Both porches were cosmetically redone. There was a lot of cleanup of stray lines about the interior before construction. Another thing, the great chimney in the back once housed an old woodburning stove. That was bricked off and a stainless steelo gas range takes its place. Although I still intend to adjust the cosmetics from time to time, I think it really turned out! Please rate. there is a link to my Facebook page of architecture and homes :)

BUT don't let that discourage you from downloading this authenticlly acurate model. It is a great house with 6 bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms, and with a uniquely interesting central atrium. I can asure you that the model is structurally correct, the dimensions are accurate, and the coloring is up to par. I admit, I don't have the intricate wall paper patterns but I used a similar color in replacement. The house looks fairly different for it has been remodeled substantially since the murders. I didn't find enough sources to make an accurate today's house but had plenty for the 1974 version. Enjoy it. Oh, yeah, it includes all built-ins (except the bar in sunroom), it remains unfurnished. description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is one building of a 6-building housing project. I modeled this tall apartment house after the famous Brewster Wheeler Housing Project in Detroit Michigan Near downtown. I understand this is the year these tall buildings along with some townhouses will be demolished by the city but I liked the designs so I modeled it. This is the tallest building in Paulwall standing at 15 stories in counting! If you are wondering about the first floor, it is sunken into the ground by a few feet. The vestibule has a few steps leading downward. No apartments on the first floor, just the second and so on up. Turn the roof layer off to see the top floor. 8 apartments, a trash room, mechanical room (empty), mail chute, stairs, and an elevator shaft. Each house has 2 small bedrooms, walk-in pantry, one bathroom, and so on. I modeled this old house using whatever photos I could find online as well as watching the videos about it. Diana Ross and the Supremes lived here for a little while. It was the first subsidized house in America for African Americans. Completed in 1952. I hope you enjoy this old house and please rate. Though the actual thing exists in Detroit, you may feel free to put it into your inner city. You can remove the apartments and make it a background object if you like :)

In light of being in the way of something this meaningful, I decided to give you something special! I'm sure a lot of you have heard of and admire the arts of Sir Frank Lloyd Wright. Quite a few have uploaded Frank Lloyd Wrights so I thought, Why not? However, I have not found anyone who's uploaded this particular house. About this house, it was built in 1940, on a steep hillface off of the beautiful Lake Mendota in Wisconsin. The construction was also unusual which consisted of stone counterforts and diagonal ship-lap siding. The home is also unsual because of the low ceilings. The first floor: 6'9Second Floor 7'6. The house was made with its exact dimentions. I used his sections, scaled floor plan, and whatever pictures I've scrounged off the internet (lots). Though the home has changed a little, I made the home as it is seen today by visitors. Take a look, even at the ceilings, fireplace, stone-lined revine, carport, and basement rafters. Upstairs has 3 small bedrooms with built-in beds and one bathroom. A particular acknowledgement would be the famous origami chairs in the living room. Although they were not in the origional plan, they were added later, sitting there today. They were modeled by my good friend, Jeff Myers (JATdesigns) however, everything else was crafted by me. Enjoy this model. The layers will make it easy for you. I hope you have as much fun looking through it as I had in making it. I have a Facebook Page now :)

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Located just north of Paulwall's downtown district, there are a number of beautifully preserved victorian houses. Few, however, remain single family homes for some were broken into apartments, some are offices for companies who bought them, and a few are abandoned. But each are unique not only to each other but to the other houses in the community. These are the houses that get photographed. For example, this one here with its intricate brick work, signiture turret, pointed arch in front, is a great example of a guilded age mansion. They do not make them like this anymore which is why people like to visit Paulwall, to see what is left of its eclectic architecture. See its fancy chimnies or the widow's walk on the roof. You even see the trapdoor hatch! Forgive this shell model for it does not yet have an interior (but will have one soon). Though, in the mean time, lots of details to see and to enjoy. You can even use it as a backdrop object for your urban neighborhood scene! Welcome to the Ransom Gillis House! Although the origin is in Brush Park, Detroit, Paulwall proudly holds a replica of it. Enjoy and please rate. I have a page on Facebook set up for architecture and Sketchup enthusiasts so check out my link below if you wish :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 It is a 40's tract house. These houses were very common in the United States in cities used mainly by the working class and incoming veterans. In this time period, there was a skyrocket in the demand for housing so many houses were needed in a short time. Tract homes were very cookie cutter so you would step out onto your porch to see a copy of your house across the street. However, the homes weren't all the same. They varied by neighborhood and time period. It was common that tract homes had 2 bedrooms but this model actually has 4. It also has 2 full bathrooms (another rare comfort)! There is a basement. I am not a fan of tract-style kitchens so I designed the kitchen. It is designed for the tabe to be right there in the kitchen. There is a wroght iron column in front along with a living room picture window. There is good clost space here. The chimney is actually the furnace vent trailing all the way to the basement. These houses most commonly found near factories or jumbled around downtown. Either way, I hope you enjoy this tract house. Please rate. For more houses and architecture, don't forget to check out my Facebook page given at the link below.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a classy additon to my collection. This southern colonial stately looking house would be a fine addition to your southern neighborhood. It has that plantation feeling with its large front colonade and massive chimneys. All around you will find classic finishes to give it a good appeal. Expensive looking too. Come on in to a tall foyer. Here, this house has a living room (or den) in front with a large family room behind (both have fire places). On your left, there is a formal dining room. Beyond are the kitchen and breakfast room. Kitchen pantry is behind the refridgerator. One chimney has the two fire places, the other chimney is the mechanical rool. This house has 3 bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms. There is a powder room off the entryway. Looking for the coat closet? It is in that little hall betwwen laundry room and garage. You get a deluxe master suite with all the fixin's. It actually takes up the entire right wing of the house! Out back is a massive wooden deck with cherry stain. A greenhouse/ sunroom is around the side I hope this house gives you a feeling of the south. I could swear I heard some bluegrass somewhere. Anyway, enjoy this classic colonial house and please rate :)

Historically a part of Lancashire, Ancoats became one of the cradles of the Industrial Revolution, and has been called the world's first industrial suburb. The area suffered accelerating economic decline from the 1930s and depopulation in the years after the Second World War, particularly during the slum clearances of the 1960s.
Since the 1990s Ancoats' industrial heritage has been recognised and this, along with its proximity to the city centre, has led to investment and the development of substantial regeneration plans.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 (Modified version)   ==============   Naqsh-e Jahan Square (Persian: میدان نقش جهان‎ Maidān-e Naqsh-e Jahān; trans: Image of the World Square), known as Imam Square (میدان امام), formerly known as Shah Square (میدان شاه), is a square situated at the center of Isfahan city, Iran. Constructed between 1598 and 1629, it is now an important historical site, and one of UNESCO's World Heritage Sites. It is 160 meters wide by 508 meters long[1] (an area of 89,600 m2). The square is surrounded by buildings from the Safavid era. The Shah Mosque is situated on the south side of this square. On the west side is the Ali Qapu Palace. Sheikh Lotf Allah Mosque is situated on the eastern side of this square and the northern side opens into the Isfahan Grand Bazaar. Today, Namaaz-e Jom'eh (the Muslim Friday prayer) is held in the Shah Mosque.

The professor had suffered from a cerebral hemorrhage and died, never returning to the train station where Hachikō was waiting. Every day for the next nine years the golden brown Akita waited at Shibuya station.------------Hachikō was given away after his master's death, but he routinely escaped, returning again and again to his old home. Eventually, Hachikō apparently realized that Professor Ueno no longer lived at the house. So he went to look for his master at the train station where he had accompanied him so many times before. Each day, Hachikō waited for the return of his owner.------------The permanent fixture at the train station that was Hachikō attracted the attention of other commuters. Many of the people who frequented the Shibuya train station had seen Hachikō and Professor Ueno together each day. They brought Hachikō treats and food to nourish him during his wait.------------  This continued for nine years with Hachikō appearing precisely when the train was due at the station.

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 7 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 I did this diamond Logo to pay homage to the 4th Doctor's Doctor Who Logo, I just updated it for my own purpose but I did not like the idea of the diamond being blank on the other side, so for a bit of fun I put Matt Smiths name there and I wanted my logo to be the same or near to it, the same color as the TARDIS.
I used 3D Text for the lettering, if you can imagine the logo as part of the new Doctor Who title sequence, I hope you can see the potential this logo could have with it spinning around at a good speed, so people can see the logo change from saying Doctor Who To Matt Smith.  Please be gentle with your comments and your rating.  I'm still learning with GoogleSketchUp 7.

description_text:
The Museo Soumaya is a private museum in Mexico City. It has over 66,000 works from 30 centuries of art including sculptures from Pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica, 19th- and 20th-century Mexican art and an extensive repertoire of works by European old masters and masters of modern western art such as Auguste Rodin, Salvador Dalí, Bartolomé Esteban Murillo and Tintoretto. It is considered one of the most complete collections of its kind.
The building is considered Postmodern, it was designed by Mexican architect Fernando Romero, engineered with Ove Arup and Frank Gehry, and finished in 2011.

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The Freedom Monument (Latvian: Brīvības piemineklis) is a memorial located in Riga, Latvia honoring soldiers killed during the Latvian War of Independence (1918–1920). It is considered an important symbol of the freedom, independence, and sovereignty of Latvia.[1]  Unveiled in 1935, the 42-metre (138 ft) high monument of granite, travertine, and copper  often serves as the focal point of public gatherings and official ceremonies in Riga. (wikipedia.org)
The sculptures and bas-reliefs of the monument, arranged in thirteen groups, depict Latvian culture and history. The core of the monument is composed of tetragonal shapes on top of each other, decreasing in size towards the top, completed by a 19-metre (62 ft) high travertine column bearing the copper figure of Liberty lifting three gilded stars. The concept for the monument first emerged in the early 1920s when the Latvian Prime Minister, Zigfrīds Anna Meierovics, ordered rules to be drawn up for a contest for designs of a memorial column. After several contests the monument was finally built at the beginning of the 1930s according to the scheme Shine like a star! submitted by Latvian sculptor Kārlis Zāle. Construction works were financed by private donations.

The earliest parols were traditionally made from simple materials like bamboo sticks, Japanese rice paper (known as papel de Hapon) or crepe paper, and a candle or coconut oil-lamp for illumination; although the present day parol can take many different shapes and forms.  The most basic parol can be easily constructed with just ten bamboo sticks, paper, and glue. These lanterns represent the Star of Bethlehem that guided the Magi, also known as the Three Wise Men or Three Kings (Tatlong Hari in Tagalog).
Puto Bumbong, Traditionally made from a special variety of heirloom sticky or glutinous rice called Pirurutong which has a distinctly purple color, soaked in salted water and dried overnight and then poured into bumbong or bamboo tubes and then steamed until done or steam rises out of the bamboo tubes. It is served topped with butter or margarine and shredded coconut mixed with sugar.
Puto bumbong is the most sought after delicacies at Christmas time. During the simbang gabi or the Christmas Eve mass, people would line up to their favorite stalls outside the church just to have a taste of this favorite Pinoy delicacies.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The red telephone kiosk has become a landmark and has its own national conservation plan. It was born in 1933 after an architectural competition, which was won by architect Georg Fasting from Bergen. The first was set up on Amerikalinjens docked in Oslo. A restored version is currently set up at near-native space (see photo). Only after the war spread this kiosk type to the rest of the country. The location of public telephone boxes always took into account the public safety and should provide easy access to a doctor, midwife, police and fire. They were an obvious staple among apartment blocks in the 60s suburbs, at railway stations and at numerous ferry ports. The public telephone kiosk was primarily a service, and profitability came in second place. The last kiosk was produced in 1995. In total it has been produced about 9,000 copies of this kind, and many are still in use. The design has remained without changes, except for the weight: The first kiosks weighed 800 kg, while later editions weighed less than half. To elaborate on the tower design, it has a geometric cylinder base that houses a large retailer store(Walmart in this case) with an elevator in the middle of the cylinder leading all the way to the roof of the structure. The roof itself resembles that of a true crown. The spire is a DNA double helix strand that has LED lighting and imagery (imaging Target Plaza south 100,000 LED's in a spiral form). The south face of the building also has a double helix pattern running from the 3rd floor to the crown, which would also have animated LED'S. I don't know the market well, but I have faith in Minneapolis. And if you guys show support for this design, who knows? Maybe OPUS will see it and consider it. So let's make this building POPULAR TWIN CITIZENS!!!DISCLAIMER: I DID NOT MAKE THE GLASS TEXTURE! THAT CREDIT GOES TO m b p. So thank him everyone. That person is awesome!

This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 A simplified model of an RTG lke those used on deep space probes by NASA.  Probes which go further than the orbit of Mars face very low levels of sunlight, making solar panels ineffective as the primary power source.
 An RTG is a decay-based nuclear power source that uses pellets of plutonium-238 to generate heat.  The heat is converted to electricity by a thermoelectric material.
RTGs have been used on the Pioneer and Voyager probes as well as newer probes like the New Horizons probe on its way to Pluto.   They provide decades of reliable power to the spacecraft systems

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The goal! The main objective of this project is to identify the original attitude of the rock movements, to translate and interpret it into a new architectural language and interior design for a contemporary house in the urban down town of the city. 
How to redefine the meaning of the contemporary house?... Grunge architecture!! Based in a previous knowledge and deep research about the rock culture, is settle a theoretical document that translates the most significant rock values, into architectural shapes and interior design language for the house. Grunge architecture transforms the traditional house into a feelings-machine with new space relations. An architectural element inspired by the punk, the hard rock and the grunge music as well. The cultural and conceptual parameters that have been influenced this kind of music-movements are the research database for this particular project.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is my train station on my layout.  A little bit of history:  when I went into the service in the 70s, my dad tossed out all my stuff while I was overseas  I guess he was afraid I would come home in a box!.  Fast forward to about 15 years ago.  I was browsing in an antique shop and I found this kit from the 50s.  I bought  it. (My old kit?) A friend of mine said not to build it cause it would decrease the value.  After several models, I built the train station.  It sees a lot of trafic.  I had to add some foundation pieces from Plastruct shapes.  It has been there ever since.  As a bonus, I have included some pictures of my layout.  They were taken with a low-res camera, so they are a  bit fuzzy.  You can see the train starion in its home.  I also included a picture of a bank robbery with the Idaho State Police car which is very valuable and my theatre.  So have fun with this,  The kit does not have stairs, which I added to the model.  This model is 90% components.  The stairs are components, you can edit them to add railings.  This a shell with floors.  Is made up of 3X 3 squares.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 15 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 I have a train station on my layout that is a modular kit.  The kit was made in the 1950s.  It has wall panels and columns that interlock.  After watching a show on cable that had a house I liked, I thought that I would  see if I could make a house of the kit components like that one.  Here it is.  The exterior has 42 columns 24X24 10' high made of extruded concrete.  The wall panels are a sandwich of stamped steel (or aluminum) powder coated white on the outside with auto enamel, a foam core, and drywall taped, textured, and painted on the inside.  Walls are capped with a 2' high parapet.  Front door has a 4' high parapet.  There is 3 bedrooms, 2 1/2 baths, kitchen, dining, and a 2 story livingroom.  The walkout basement is finished.  Highlights: cutout in the Master Bedroom overlooking the living room,  mirrored closet doors, a column in a corner of the master shower, and a wood stove in the Basement.  The Library has a pull-down projector screen.  Finally, a 2-car garage in the house footprint, which measures 51' X 30'.  Exterior walls are components.  You can copy them and make your own house if you want to.  These are only one width of many walls in the kit.  Front door is interactive, I left it open for you.  Close it via Tools>Interact if you want to.  Bob

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is one of the employees cabins at Sequoia Nat'l Park.  It for the married employees.  There are about 6 of these cabins.  Us single people stay in small cabins in the employees housing area.  This is an exact copy of the floor plan, I just changed the wall materials and roof.  The cabins were built in the 1920s.  They are over-built because there can be as much as 20' of snow in the winter.  One of my jobs was opening the cabin in the spring and closing it in the fall.  The maintainance crew stripped the interior after each season, leaving only what is in there now.  Emplyees who lived there had to scrounge for any extra items they wanted.  Even tho it has been 30 years since I worked there, the cabins may still be there.  Main floor is the living area; there is a sleeping loft above the bath, kitchen and dining area.

Its construction began as a monastery in 1088 at a time when Alfonso VI reigned. Then he became fortress due to the threat of the Christian kingdom and possible entries of Muslims by the Alcantara bridge. With the total expulsion of Muslims from the Iberian Peninsula, the fortress gradually lost its defense function relegated to oblivion. After various vicissitudes, and under threat of demolition in 1874 was named a Historic-Artistic National. Today, in the XXI century, the castle is completely restored and after serving successively as junior college, home of the Castile-La Mancha and university residence, now does as a youth hostel in the Regional Government of Castile-La Mancha and venue for courses and conferences. description_text:
Mexico City's first skyscraper, the Torre Latinoamericana!
MiniWorld celebrates Mexico City with this free model. With 188 m or 597 ft; 44 stories finished in 1956, it was the first skyscraper to be succesfully built on a highly-seismic location. It's name comes from the Seguros Latinoamericana insurance company, headquartered in the building. It was designed by architect Augusto H. Álvarez. This historical and modernist building is a symbol of Mexico City and has become a landmark. Have you seen the city from it's lookout?
MiniWorld is the collection of 3D printable models of landmarks of the world. All our models are made from scratch by hand and brain, please give credit, it's all about spreading culture!
This model is support-free and very easy to print. Use a sewing pin as antena!

description_text: This is a 4 sided glass pyramid with a glass sphere inside with a solid cube inside of that. Shapes within shapes. I was not too suer if I could pull of something like this. I encourage you all to download this model to take a closer look and you will find that there is exactly a cube within the sphere. I did the pyramid as a speerate model, then the sphere and the cube all in sketchup, then I imported the cube first to put that inside of the sphere, using the scaling tool, then I saved the two as one whole model and then I imported combined cube inside a sphere model, scaled it down to fit it inside the pyramid and then to adjust the sphere and cube model to the right size and line everything up as best possible, so when you zoom in, the path will take you to the sphere and into it to face the solid cube iside.

It sits in an old neighborhood lined with many, many others very similar to it, all looking alike, a few hundred houses in a few neighborhoods, where you'd see these homes from the 30's and the 40's. They sit just east and southeast of the Paulwall downtown district. The old houses are fairly cheap, certainly not the best neighborhood, the side of town where window bars are common although are absent from this model. Though the houses in long rows look a lot alike, there are some variations such as sidings, some brick, some frame. Some have 2 bedrooms, some have 3. This house has 2 bedrooms at back however, some of the homes have the bedrooms on the side. All of the houses have only wone bathroom and a lightly pitched roof. A lot of these houses retained their retro kitchen appliances and they all have basements. Some perks to living in this neighborhood is that it is blocks away from the Paulwall College and near the main library as well as some shopping. These streets are lined with fully grown oak trees  I hope you enjoy this postwar starter house and please rate.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This house features a full interior! This is sort of a small house with 3 bedrooms and two bathrooms. The house has a split-level floorplan and a two car garage. Though your laundry station only features the washer, dryer, and overhead cabinets, there is a vaccum cleaner closet right next to it. There are generous closets throughout the house. The master bedroom features dual walk-in closets. The kitchen is chef's choice with stainless steel appliances, breakfast bar, and a pantry behind the refridgerator. The coat closet is the bigger closet beyond the pantry. Dining room in front with wainscotting. There is a pergola out back. The basement door is in the garage. You will find other details too such as the hot water heater. This is the type of house you would find in the average midwestern suburbs! I designed this one myself made for a narrow lot. Enjoy this house and please rate. description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 MY 100th MODEL!!! In light of being in the way of something this meaningful, I decided to give you something special! I'm sure a lot of you have heard of and admire the arts of Sir Frank Lloyd Wright. Quite a few have uploaded Frank Lloyd Wrights so I thought, Why not? However, I have not found anyone who's uploaded this particular house. About this house, it was built in 1940, on a steep hillface off of the beautiful Lake Mendota in Wisconsin. The construction was also unusual which consisted of stone counterforts and diagonal ship-lap siding. The home is also unsual because of the low ceilings. The first floor: 6'9Second Floor 7'6. The house was made with its exact dimentions. I used his sections, scaled floor plan, and whatever pictures I've scrounged off the internet (lots). Though the home has changed a little, I made the home as it is seen today by visitors. Take a look, even at the ceilings, fireplace, stone-lined revine, carport, and basement rafters. Upstairs has 3 small bedrooms with built-in beds and one bathroom. A particular acknowledgement would be the famous origami chairs in the living room. Although they were not in the origional plan, they were added later, sitting there today. They were modeled by my good friend, Jeff Myers (JATdesigns) however, everything else was crafted by me. Enjoy this model. The layers will make it easy for you. I hope you have as much fun looking through it as I had in making it. I have a Facebook Page now :)

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Hamilton GO Centre is a GO Transit railway and bus station located at Hunter Street East and Hughson Street South in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. The Centre in the facility's name refers to how, unlike other GO stations, it doubles as a regional bus terminal for private intercity coach carriers including Greyhound and Coach Canada. It opened in 1933 as the head office and the Hamilton station of the Toronto, Hamilton and Buffalo Railway. Passenger service on the TH&B was discontinued on April 26, 1981, and the TH&B merged into the Canadian Pacific Railway in 1987, leaving the facility completely unused. In order to better connect GO Transit service to Hamilton's CBD, improve the interface with the Hamilton Street Railway, and consolidate train and bus services at a single site, renovations were undertaken to convert the TH&B station into the Hamilton GO Centre. The new facility, designed by Garwood-Jones & Hanham Architects opened on April 30, 1996.

The deposit was discovered in 1912 in the village of Mala Pereshchepina (20 km from Poltava, Ukraine) by a boy shepherd who literally stumbled over a golden vessel and fell into what is sometimes believed to be the grave of Kuvrat, the founder of Great Bulgaria and father of Asparuh, the founder of the First Bulgarian Empire. The hoard, first described by Makarenko, was extracted under the supervision of Count Aleksey Bobrinsky, a renowned archaeologist, who published its description in 1914. Although Kuvrat's link to the hoard seems certain (see below), the exact nature of the site, grave or treasure, is disputed, since neither human remains nor indisputable evidence of a funeral device are reported to have been found.
The hoard contains more than 800 pieces, now preserved in the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg. There are 19 silver vessels and 16 gold vessels, including a striking rhyton and remains of another.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 It is described in Title I of Law 4/1985, of June 3, the shield, the flag and the Day of Extremadura. description_text: Since its inception was the main church of medieval history. Its construction began in the late thirteenth century, however the bulk of the building was built in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, in Gothic, sober and elegant style. The architectural structure is irregular due to the building of a temple with different architectural bases. It has three naves of which the central is the largest, made of masonry; the pillars on which sit the vaults are Gothic, two side chapels by the presbytery, two other adjacent on the side of the Epistle, and Renaissance choir. Inside they deserve special attention the door of the sacristy, the sixteenth century by Alonso de Torralba in the year 1525, built with arch on pilasters platerescas; the apse of the XV century, is covered by the vault, it is situated to one side the chapel of Christ and across the chapel of San Miguel, sixteenth century; the altarpiece of the main altar, Renaissance work in cedarwood Roque Balduque the year 1551; Backlog Holy Water, made of marble in the fourteenth century; numerous gravestones, tombs and sarcophagi; as well as a rich collection of liturgical objects from the XV to XIX. At the foot of the tower is the bronze statue of San Pedro de Alcántara, sculpted by Pérez Comendador.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The Four Worlds is a building in Spijkenisse, Netherlands. The residential building is ontwopren by Mei Architects and is part of the new district Elements in Spijkenisse. The building consists of four parts, which are two connected towers. The lower tower is 50 meters, the upper 70. The building has 22 floors and a total of 253 homes. In December 2008 the building reached its highest point, to be thus (temporarily) the tallest building in Spijkenisse. The Four Worlds is divided into four sections or worlds. These worlds vary in appearance, both in front and inside. Each world has a different name: Coast. This world is covered with a white facade and comprises 65 apartments. City. This world is coated with a light gray facade and contains 86 apartments. This world, this is the greatest. Village. This world is covered with a dark gray facade and comprises 66 apartments. Metropole. This world is covered with glass and contains 36 apartments. This world, this is the smallest.

description_text: Photo 3D model of the Tower of Los Velasco in Medina de Pomar. Burgos. Castilla-Leon. Spain. The citadel or castle of Medina de Pomar Velasco, also called The Towers of Medina is one of the largest and most spectacular medieval fortifications in the province of Burgos. It was built by the family Velasco from 1370 for residential use as stately palace. Its structure is Allemandes two towers linked by a lower and shallower section, where two doors open on opposite walls. The towers show various bays, well kind of loophole or mullioned Gothic traces. Inside the Alcázar de los Velasco, there are many dependencies with traces of plaster and other Moorish decorations, perfectly suited to the fourteenth century, where kings and nobles Christians had succumbed to the luxury and sensuality of Moorish aesthetics. (Arteguias.com)

description_text: Standing at the centre of the southern enclosure, this listed fountain was inaugurated on 25 May 1846 for the Queen's twenty-seventh birthday. Designed by A.H.Wilds, it was financed jointly by John Cordy Burrows and a public subscription, and was cast at the Eagle Foundry in Gloucester Road.    Dimensions of the fountain  It stands thirty-two feet high, with two shallow basins supported by three cast-iron dolphins above a large pool, and has a base of sarsen stones which were found in the Steine by workmen in 1823. To commemorate the inauguration, local musician Charles Coote composed the Fountain Quadrilles.    In 1990 the top of the fountain was removed for restoration EDIT: Transparent water fixed. You should now see details beneath.

description_text: The Duke of Yorks Picture House is the oldest continuously operating purpose built cinema in Britain. It was also one of the first cinemas in the world.   It opened on 22nd September 1910 and the building remains largely unaltered. It was built on the site of the Amber Ale Brewery. The architects were Clayton and Black. It houses a single screen with 283 seats, including a luxury balcony. There is also a cafe/bar upstairs. The Duke of Yorks is a Grade II listed building.   The giant model legs on the top are one of the more eye catching elements of the building, these came from the 'Not the Moulin Rouge Theatre' in Oxford.      Well worth a visit for a different kind of cinema experience.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 At that time the townspeople with the contribution of Count Csáky built the first stone theatre (1776) in approximately the same place as today's historical building of the SND. The importance of the city declines in the 19th century. The city theatre is rented by German and later Hungarian companies.               In 1886 the new building of the City Theatre is opened. It is built in Neo-Renaissance style according to the design of Helmer and Fellner’s Vienna theatre architecture company. The opening performance is Erkel’s ’Bánk bán’ presented by the Budapest National Theatre Company. Verism quickly triumphs in this building, in the last year of the century Bruno Walter gains experience here as a teacher. At the beginning of the new century the Brno Opera presents a wide cross-section through the Czech classical opera and, for the first time in Bratislava, Tchaikovski’s ’Eugen Onegin’ and ’The Queen of Spades’.               In 1919 Bratislava becomes a part of the Czechoslovak Republic. In 1920 the professional Slovak National Theatre starts to work in the building of the City Theatre. It has theatre and opera companies. It starts its activities with the premiere of Smetana’s ’The Kiss’ on March 1, 1920.

description_text: At the core of today's building are two Gothic houses built later during the 15th century that were directly connected to the mineshaft the vein SPITALERI. At the turn of the 16th and 17th centuries were structurally unified storey palace to house miners waldburgrovského Fritz von Friedenlieb. Later she was rebuilt in Baroque style. Since the beginning of the 19th century, the inner courtyard of the house have hosted urban balls, there was kresliareň, collections and library of the Academy. Radical was his rebuilding in the last third of the 19th century, when it served as an administrative building, seat of the rector therefore Mining and Forestry Academy. From this transformation comes Renaissance facade, richly articulated, in addition to a rich plastic decoration also applied sgraffito. At present, it houses the Slovak Mining Archives.

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Most Apollo (literally Apollo Bridge, provisionally known as Most Košická during construction, after the street leading to it) in Bratislava is a road bridge over the Danube in the capital of Slovakia.
The bridge was opened to the public on September 5, 2005. It is named for the Apollo (modern successor: Slovnaft) oil refinery which was situated on the left river bank in this area before World War II. Its curved lines, inclined arches arches and virtual absence of right angles make the geometric shape of the bridge very sophisticated. In an unprecedented maneuver, the 5,240-ton steel structure, spanning 231 meters, was rotated across the river from its construction site on the left bank into its final position on a pillar 40 meters from the right bank. The Apollo Bridge was the only European project named one of five finalists for the 2006 Outstanding Civil Engineering Achievement Award (OPAL Award) by the American Society of Civil Engineers.

description_text: Originally ground gothic house from the 14th century in which the city council met, was rebuilt in 1488 on a storey building. In early 16th century the building was erected chapel. Anne, which was demolished in the 18th century and in its place was built a sculpture of the Virgin Mary. Hall got its present form in the years 1787 - 1788. At the entrance to the town hall is located plaque, commemorating the entry of Banská Štiavnica on the list of world cultural and natural heritage.

description_text:
This is my model of a round expanding folding table or "Fletcher Capstan Table".
The idea with the table is that a small round table can be expanded into a large round table by expanding the pizza slice-shaped table parts outwards, and wedges and a middle “star” will come up from inside the table and together they form a large round table.
The model does not have the inside mechanics to make it actually work. If I in the future will take it upon myself to make a working model a few of the measurements will probably have to be changed to make it work. But as it is, it is at least quite a beautiful table, if I may say it so myself.
The a model made in SolidWorks and it is an assembly made up out of many parts.The download includes two assemblies. One of the table in its compressed form, and one in its expanded form. All the parts and the assemblies are included in SolidWorks (.sldprt and .sldasm) and also as step-files.
If you have any questions or requests about the table, please contact me.

description_text:
Buckyballs are popular shapes for geodesic domes.  
All the edges have the same length and only one type of vertex.  
The each vertex connects two hexagons with one pentagon.  
A real dome is going to be more complicated because you will want more floor area than one face.  
Joining or extending balls is harder again because most faces are at strange angles.  
Here is one way to add an extension.  
There are simpler ways but this keeps the faceted look of the dome.  
The end of the tube part could be repeated as desired.  
Instead of a single dome more could be added as required. The most likely use would be as a greenhouse or shade house.  

Also I'm uploading some fused bucky balls to show how a cluster can be made.  

I should point out these shape are not exact. I'm using sketchup which is lousy for this kind of thing.

description_text: This is not about a specific model, it's about my python/SolidPython script that creates arbitrary grid trays (with rounded bottoms so there's no corners), useful for organizing lots of small items. Especially nice for creating board game organizers. The script is attached, it is called "generic_tray.py".  You run it from the command line with the grid dimensions and it will spit out a .scad file and [optionally] a .stl file.   It will also show you the [approximate] volume of each bin. ------ USAGE  ------  ***ALL UNITS ARE MILLIMETERS***  The tray will be specified by the dimensions of each row/column, provided as two arrays. The example screenshot shows the terminal after running the tool.  Use the following command-line call to create the example in the screenshot (x-axis always first).  python generic_tray.py [40,60,35,20] [30,40]Make sure there are no spaces before or after the commas in the lists:  You can add extra args to adjust floor- and wall-thickness, bin depth and how rounded you want the bins to be on the bottom:    `python generic_tray.py [40,60,35,20] [30,40] --depth=55 --outfile=mytray.scad` Type the following to see all options:     `python generic_tray.py --help` *** IF YOU DON'T WANT/CAN'T DO THE COMMAND-LINE THING, then follow the directions towards where CLI_OPTIONS and CLI_ARGS are set in the script.  You can remove all the CLI_* code and simply hardcode the tray size into this script so you only have to double-click it to generate the SCAD file. This will automatically generate a .scad file that can be loaded into  OpenSCAD.  It will always ask if you want to also generate the .stl file, which can be loaded into most 3D printing slicers, but this can be very slow unless you are using --round=0.  It is recommended, if you are tweaking the tray dimensions and checking resultant bin volumes, to always skip creating the STL (type nothing, press enter), until you are happy with it, then re-run the last command and type  "y" before enter to generate the .stl.   *NOTE*:  Read the README.txt, and note that if you need precise bin sizes, calibrate your printer using my calibration cubes and create a caldata.py file.SETUP ------  The requirements to use generic_tray.py is:  Python 2.X  OpenSCAD  SolidPython (python wrapper around OpenSCAD)  (1) You must install the latest Python 2.X, currently python 2.7.8    if you are in Windows (comes installed by default in Linux & OSX)     DO NOT install python 3.X -- this only works with python2.X: https://www.python.org/downloads/(2) You need to have OpenSCAD installed.  The script always generates     a .scad file, which requires OpenSCAD for viewing and/or converting      to STL format.  In Ubuntu, install openscad through the pkg manager:          sudo apt-get install openscad      Otherwise, download it from here: http://www.openscad.org/downloads.html    Even if you don't use the OpenSCAD application, you must have OpenSCAD      available so that the script can use it to generate the STL files.     The script assumes that "openscad" program/exe is in your PATH.  If      it isn't, you may need to adjust the generic_tray.py script to call the     full path to openscad or openscad.exe.  (3) SolidPython is required for the generic_tray.py script to be able to      generate .scad files.  Generally speaking, you can use OpenSCAD by      itself to make 3D models, but the SCAD "language" is weak and extremely     limited in functionality.   SolidPython is a python library that lets       you create your models in python (using proper variables, loops, etc),       and it generates simple SCAD for you. Get SolidPython from here: https://github.com/SolidCode/SolidPython    You can simply copy the "solid" directory into your project directory (so     that the generic_tray.py script can call "import solid" and it will find      ./solid/__init__.py).  Or within the outer SolidPython directory, you can       run "sudo python setup.py install".  This will install the "solid" directory      into your global site-packages directory so that it will be available no      matter where you run generic_tray.py.

description_text:
OpenForge  
=========  
These strips are designed to let tiles with walls along their edge (instead of on top of a square) to be able to but up against each other.  You only need these buffers if you are using the OpenForge edge series.  

There are three basic sets here:  

* Lines  
The lines are the same length as the squares (1x-4x) of the squares on the tiles.  
* corners  
The corners are the same length as the squares (1x-4x) of teh squares on the tiles  plus a hub that's wth width of a wall from a wall tile.  They can have 1-4 spokes coming off that hub.  For most people anything past 3x length with 3 or more spokes is unprintably large.  
* corner walls  
Corner walls are the same as corners, except they also have a wall height spoke going up.  These are designed to fill in gaps between walls butted up against each other.  In most cases, only 1 or 2 spokes are actually useful, but all are uploaded for completeness.  

=============

description_text:
OpenForge  
=========  
Dungeon edge diagonal tiles designed to be compatible with Dwarven Forge dungeon tiles.  This set also includes half diagonal floor tiles (with built in edge buffer) for dealing with diagonals that have playing area on both sides of the wall.  

The smooth set can be used for any number of things. Look at the Smooth floor tile set for ideas. There, I've done concrete, ice and dirt. Here I've done concrete.   

These tiles are designed to line their wall up with walls from tiles butted up against their neighbours.  These are designed to be used on the edge of the map or to give more usable space for the play area, particularly for 1x hallways which would be impossible to fit mins in unless the wall was moved.  Because the wall now takes up some space, you will need to use [edge buffers] in some places to get the tiles to lay out properly.  

Compatible tiles/walls in this series are tagged with OpenForge

A touchscreen is an electronic visual display that the user can control through simple or multi-touch gestures by touching the screen with a special stylus/pen and-or one or more fingers. Some touchscreens use an ordinary or specially coated gloves to work while others use a special stylus/pen only. The user can use the touchscreen to react to what is displayed and to control how it is displayed (for example by zooming the text size).The touchscreen enables the user to interact directly with what is displayed, rather than using a mouse, touchpad, or any other intermediate device (other than a stylus, which is optional for most modern touchscreens).(Wikipedia)
Infrared acrylic projectionA translucent acrylic sheet is used as a rear projection screen to display information. The edges of the acrylic sheet are illuminated by infrared LEDs, and infrared cameras are focused on the back of the sheet. Objects placed on the sheet are detectable by the cameras. When the sheet is touched by the user the deformation results in leakage of infrared light, which peaks at the points of maximum pressure indicating the user's touch location. Microsoft's PixelSense tables use this technology.(Wikipedia)

Tower 42 was built in 1980 and took 6 year to build. The building has 47 floors and stands at a fairly impressive 183m tall. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Requested by Cesey A.K.A. Air Transat. Original AC 762 by WilliamT. The 767-200 was the original model and entered service with United Airlines in 1982. The type has been used primarily by mainline U.S. carriers for domestic routes between major hub centers such as Los Angeles to Washington. The 767-200 was the first aircraft to be used on transatlantic ETOPS flights, beginning with TWA on February 1, 1985 under 90-minute diversion rules. Deliveries for the variant totaled 128 aircraft. There were 63 passenger and freighter conversions of the model in airline service as of July 2012. The type's competitors included the Airbus A300 and A310. The 767-200 ceased production in the late 1980s due to being superseded by the extended-range 767-200ER. Some early 767-200s were subsequently upgraded to extended-range specification. In 1998, Boeing began offering 767-200 conversions to 767-200SF [Special Freighter] specification for cargo use, and Israel Aerospace Industries has been licensed to perform cargo conversions since 2005. The conversion process entails the installation of a side cargo door, strengthened main deck floor, and added freight monitoring and safety equipment. The 767-200SF is positioned as a replacement for the Douglas DC-8 freighter.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Keflavik International Airport {Icelandic: Keflavíkurflugvöllur} [IATA: KEF, ICAO: BIKF], also known as Reykjavík-Keflavík Airport, is the largest airport in Iceland and the country’s main hub for international transportation. It is situated 1.7 NM {3.1 km; 2.0 mi} west of Keflavík and 50 km [31 m] south-west of Reykjavík. The airport has two runways and the airport area is about 25 sq. km {9.7 sq. mi}. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Chapel of St. Fabian and Sebastian in Letovanić first mentioned in 1729 as the cemetery chapel to be rebuld with original lumber in 1771 on it's present location, painted ceiling cassettes were also moved. It was built as a single-space structure with a polygonal sanctuary in the shape of the ship and slender belltower over front. Above the entrance is a wooden choir, and the floor is paved with bricks. The interior is vaulted Pot vault. Small baroque altar was brought from the old chapel, and there are  pictures and statues of St. Sebastian, St. Roch and St. Florian on wooden, baroque canon tables. Behind the altar is a wooden crucifix, which may have originated in the 17th In the early 20th century the chapel's exterior were partly rebuild with new boards and mortar, and the windows increased. This renewal removed the old ceiling. Recently, front porch was added, while the facade restored to its original condition. The chapel is in good shape. The building is protected as the monument of Croatian cultural heritage

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 7 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This model is my very first attempt of doing a Tardis control room with a TARDIS Console, I know there are far better models than this, I used what was available to me and what I was able to do to create the console controls
I do not know how to make domed shapes or do wires, so I used different shapes and try to be consistent with the pattern layout, only two panels are slightly different, but that is because I wanted it to be that way.    Other than this, I was inventive putting roundals into the base of the TARDIS Console, which I do not think that has been done before, certainly not in Doctor Who console History.
I experimented with having a rod inside the Time Rotor, I made it a hexagon shaped one, as I felt that added a better extra dimension than a cylinder rod, the whole control room and console follows a pattern, of circles and hexagons, the roundals are randomly placed and of random sizes.
They are meant to be that way, adding what I feel that cookie style befitting of any Doctor, the console is almost like the Peter Davison/Colin Baker/Sylvester McCoy's TARDIS Console, I even put roundals on the door frame of the Interior door.  I wanted to have a metalic look to the console, some of what I call touch plates, also nob controls are meant to be sort of organic in nature.

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 PLEASE RATE!
A fairly acurate and highly detailed model of the Texas School Book Depository as it appeared in 1963 at the time of the Kennedy Assassination.  Includes a basic interior of the 6th floor, and sniper's nest the area where Lee Harvey Oswald is believed to have shot at President John F. Kennedy (this is disputed by conspiracy theorists).
The depository now is used for county administrative offices and houses the Sixth Floor Museum.   It appears somewhat different today, as the loading dock area has been removed and the Hertz billboard on the roof is also no longer in place.   The fround floor has also been renovated and an addition has been added to the rear of the building.
I will continue to improve the acuracy and detial of this model in the future.  PLEASE RATE!  A lot of work went into this.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is a virtual model of a card model that I have had since 1987.  It was published by Schreiber-Bogen in Germany.  You could say that is took me 25 years to make this model!   This is actually 2 models; the bare bones one above, and the enhanced one via the link at the bottom.  This small castle is part of a larger set of models.  It follows the model's measurements for a 1 inch = 16 feet scale. (Actual scale: 1:150)  The angles are correct as well.  The ground floor has 2 rooms in the main building and the garage, the entry tower has a storage room.  (More towers and staircases!)  The main floor has an Ell-shaped room with the livingroom in one leg, the kitchen and dining in the other leg.  The next floor, level 2, has 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, and a laundry.  The entry tower has several floors.  There is a spiral stairs in the larger tower, an elevator in the smaller tower.  The entry tower has a drawbridge, non-functual of course.  This represents an old castle that has been 'modernized'.  Exterior still has places where the stucco has fallen off, revealing the stone beneath.  The enhanced version has bathrooms, kitchen, and other 'stuff', including a hole in the bottom of the bay over the drawbridge.  This is used to drop things, such as boiling oil, on pesky salesmen!  TY DE for the doors and doorframes.  Both versions have a secret staircase.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 A (fictional) couple found an old fortress on E-Bay.  Fortunately they did not get sniped and they got it.  What they found was a roofless shell.  Some trusses and Stressskin panels took care of the roof problem.  Old beams made floor supports.  Since this was similar to Barcaldine Castle in Argyll (wherever that is), they had an example to follow.  Kept the 4' thick exterior walls, but carved out closets and niches.  New windows, doors.  Got lucky, an old cast iron sink fit into one of the window recesses.  kept the old spiral stairs but carved out new stairs in the walls.  To see the thickness of the walls, turn off all layers but 0, then turn on Hidden, then Main Floor, then 2nd floor layers.  There are more faces in hidden layer, this is normal.  Turn all layers on except Hidden  and you are back to normal.  Scenes are provided for starting points.  Have fun, Bob

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Back in 1985 me and some computer geeks made a text-based DOS game. I made a blueprint of the castle. Maze has direction arrows for guidance if you get lost.  There is a throne room, his and hers suites on the 4th Level, a jail and interrogation room in the basement, and servants quarters in the attic.  3rd Level has the guest rooms.  From the Entry Hall the Living Room is on the right, the Dining room is on the left.  Have fun, Bob

General changes:  removed half of the stairs, added 6 stop elevator,  pool in courtyard, hillside excavated to rear basement wall with outside door to game room, windows in game room and wine cellar.   Bob

Had this in my office for a couple of months just wondering what exterior I would put on it.  Well, here it is. Upstairs changed the front left Bedroom into 2 Baths and a Closet and made the old Bathroom into the Laundry.  Finally, tacked a 2-car Garage onto the rear.  Interior stairs to the cellar is replace by the trap door in the Garage.  Pocket doors downstairs are closed via layers.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 These are the walls for the Victorian House upper attic.  Instructions:  Save to a folder, open the High-Victorian house, then import these wall into the house.  Have already done it - it works.  It actually went where it was supposed to!  Component axis is at the front left corner on the floor template- opposite from view.  It should drop right in. Turn off layers above attic and Shadows first, though.  Neat trick: create' attic walls' layer and keep this on that layer.  This way you can stand in the attic and turn off and on the walls to compare the space allocation.  Deleted wall ends, floor, and tops to eliminate z-fighting.  You can edit component to add doors, plumbing, etc.  Door is in component listing.  Used Wheat for the wall colour- I painted the attic to match.  I use Sketchup for Dummies to help me.  Very useful.  Bob Update:  installed these walls into the attic - see Victorain House with attic- for those people who may not want to do this.  Axis is off by 1/16 inch.  Move it forward 1/16" or so.  Made a component out of the floor, so it should have fit.  Just in the wrong place.  Oops!

Originally a military outpost, the round corner towers housed the enlisted men, the central tower the officers, with the head honcho on the top floor with the corner turrets.   The mess hall was in the basement. Then someone converted it into residential quarters.  Now it is empty, they took the doors, cabinets, plumbing fixtures and any thing else that was not nailed down, even the carpets!  Some one can add those if they want to.  Cabinet locations are the gray areas on the walls. The hideous colours remain.  The bridge can be lowered or raised via layers.  Additions house the greenhouse, the laundry and bath, and the kitchen and dining.  There is a BBQ in the kitchen.  5 bedrooms, 3.5 baths and an enormous basement.  A ramp was cut into the moat wall for access to the garage. Note: This is not geo located.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This kit house dates from 1883.  The kit sold for $4000.  I don't know what that is in today's dollars.  It was built on the East River.  Originally the kitchen was in the basement with a dumbwaiter to the dining room above via stacked pantries. Updates include: the cellar, which had the heating boiler, has been turned into a garage, the original diningroom has been converted into a kitchen with a breakfast area, the library is the new dining room, and the old kitchen in the basement is a flex room.  Upstairs, the small bedroom at the front of the hall is now the master bedroom bath.  A new closet is in bedroom 3, the lower attic bedroom.  The rest of the house is pretty much the same.  The upper attic is used for storage, originally the servants quarters.  An old back porch was converted into a laundry and the pantry into a bathroom.  The original stone foundation remains with a new block foundation under the old porch.  This house may be still in existance.  The plans include a complete materials list.  Minus foundation and paint.  It is from a Victorian house design book dated 1884.  Use the view/play to walk thru the house.  I just updated it a little bit.  Thanks, Paul for the trick with the pocket doors.  Use the layers to turn them off or on.  Bob Historical update:  Look up High-Victorian House for a Bay of East River 1883 on web search for the original elevation and floor plans.  Haven't found the actual house yet.

Build Green,
Scotty

description_text: This model is only detailed in the areas that pertains to my cruise over the holidays.  From Leon, Nicaragua comes the journey to the roof of the cathedral.  Up a spiral stairs in the right rear corner of the courtyard,  across a narrow balcony to a second set of stairs. (crowded with tourists!)  These stairs in the cathedral go up to the roof.  Halfway up the top step turns left 90 degrees into a ledge.  The second half goes to the roof from that ledge.  Needless to say, it was narrow, dark, and scary.  The 2 roofs are barrel vaulted with a valley between them.  The outside one goes to the corner tower roof, here represented by the covered area on the 3rd floor terrace.  What a view!  No railings except on the tower roof, which had  round dome on the roof top.  This cathedral was built in the 15th century.  Most of the 2 story buildings are a block square with a courtyard in the middle.  The show side usually is white stucco with a colured band on the bottom.  The other sides are raw concrete.  Grilles are on the main floor windows.  The fountain is a simplified version of one in Cartagena Columbia.  The corner watchtower is typical.  The master bath vanity (here doubled up) and shower doors come from a Fort Lauderdale, FL. hotel.  Leon is a Unesco World Heritage site.  Search' Basilica Catredral de la Asuncion de Leon' here.  There is an excellent model of the cathedral.  The courtyard is 4-sided, however.  Google Earth also has pictures of it in Leon, Nicaragua.

The 767-200 was the original model and entered service with United Airlines in 1982. The type has been used primarily by mainline U.S. carriers for domestic routes between major hub centers such as Los Angeles to Washington. The 767-200 was the first aircraft to be used on transatlantic ETOPS flights, beginning with TWA on February 1, 1985 under 90-minute diversion rules. Deliveries for the variant totaled 128 aircraft. There were 63 passenger and freighter conversions of the model in airline service as of July 2012. The type's competitors included the Airbus A300 and A310. The 767-200 ceased production in the late 1980s due to being superseded by the extended-range 767-200ER. Some early 767-200s were subsequently upgraded to extended-range specification. In 1998, Boeing began offering 767-200 conversions to 767-200SF [Special Freighter] specification for cargo use, and Israel Aerospace Industries has been licensed to perform cargo conversions since 2005. The conversion process entails the installation of a side cargo door, strengthened main deck floor, and added freight monitoring and safety equipment. The 767-200SF is positioned as a replacement for the Douglas DC-8 freighter.

The gear jam problem was because the airline repair crew didnt check the plane for 2 months, resulting in the moss growing inside the mechanism. When the plane took off, the captain noticed a strange sound when he was getting the gear up. When the plane started climbing to 30,000 feet {flight from Sanaa to New York with a transition at Madrid}, the plane`s gear mechanism started producing strange sounds, until finally the gear fell unto the landing gear doors. The doors were bumped, mechanism fully unworkable, and fuselage heavily damaged. The front gear doors also became bumped and also damaged the fuselage. Pilots, passngers, and crew members noticed the following, and there was a serious gap in the floor of the interior. Electricity went off. They were landing according to the runway lights and PAPI system. The plane was approaching runway 36L. When the plane tilted to match the runway heading, the landing gear, damaged another part of the fuselage hitting the control ropes. Done. The plane is uncontrolable. When the passengers and crew began running to the opposite side of the plane, the landing gear tilted more. Then, the plane finally became controlable, but it was too late. The plane started hitting the ground with the wing, and the ailerons fixed on place to nose down. Then, the plane catched fire and exploded in 13.2 seconds.

description_text: Montánchez Castle is a true example of what were the castles of the Reconquista in the Middle Ages. For the formation of the group of buildings it seems to be that it was a fortress, from which came the walls that surrounded the Old Village. Today, the castle is characterized by its dominant location, the irregular layout and overlapping volumes and curtains. The alternation of Moors and Christians in its domain allowed the addition of architectural elements of Christian typology of the early Muslim work; this time persist three tanks and part of their path. Later, under the administration of the Order of Santiago, repairs and additions were substantial, focusing these on the walls and screed lifting several enclosures and fences surround. The main body of the castle is in the highest point of the land. The Keep has in its interior with several outbuildings, such as a camera, the armory, a noble room on the lower floor and a barn. At the entrance of the enclosure it was built a chapel.

description_text:
SummaryA.K.A. a Pythagorean cup.
InstructionsThis was printed as a test object to demonstrate how bell siphons work for aquaponics systems.  It will need to be water and air tight, so print it with 4 shells at .5 single wall thickness.  If your printer has a different wall thickness, download the .scad and adjust accordingly.
Print one tray and one bell, then you might want to do some finishing on the parts to make sure they're watertight.  Then the bell sits in the hex shaped cutout in the tray, with the holes down by the floor of the tray.
Begin to fill it with water... it will fill normally, until the water level gets to the top of the inner pipe, at which point all of the water will run out through the hole in the bottom of the tray.
This effect is useful for aquaponic and hydroponic systems, where a passive mechanism is needed to repeatedly flood and drain grow tables.

description_text:
I have designed this small electric vehicle to meet my personal mobility demands in high density urban conditions. It is by all means a girl's point of view in terms of styling and design. I have tried to create a feeling of feminine and tough look at the same time. For me this is how the women are in the modern society.

I was driven by the concept of creating a greener environment with no tailpipe emissions. The small size of the vehicle (L1900mm x W1200mm x H 1800mm) is also economical to manufacture.

The car can park at very high densities and accommodates one passenger. Rear compartment provides storage for groceries, baggage and a place for hydrogen reservoir. It is designed for short trips inside the city, with a maximum speed of 80 km/h.

The vehicle is equipped with PEM (Proton exchange membrane) fuel-cell battery, which is located in the floor of the vehicle. Exchangeable reservoir with 4kg hydrogen is placed at the rear bottom of the vehicle (1 kg of hydrogen is enough for 100km roughly). Such a placement helps to keep the center of mass low, and also contributes to cooling of the battery. 
The vehicle is powered by two electric motors 30 kW each, attached to front wheels.

description_text:
This rug was designed in 1954 by Italian architect Gio Ponti for his private home in Milan. 
From molteni.it:"Giovanni “Gio” Ponti, (Milan, November 18, 1891 - Milan, September 16, 1979), is one of the Italian masters of architecture. He was also a designer and essayist and one of the most important of the twentieth century. Other than the great architectural works which carry his unmistakable signature, he created a vast amount of work in the furniture sector. This is demonstrated in his three Milanese houses which were fully furnished in the "Ponti" style. The houses in via Randaccio, 1925, Casa Laporte in via Brin, 1926 and the last in via Dezza, in 1957 is an "expression" of his home design ideas. Gio Ponti was an Italian promoter of industrial design and introduced the idea of interior furnishing ranges produced as being a "sophisticated," economic, "democratic" and modern. Molteni&C managed a reissuing project of furniture and furnishings designed by Gio Ponti for products for these private homes and limited editions. After a long journey of research, selection and study of prototypes, the collection was exhibited at the Salone del Mobile 2012. This was thanks to the cooperation and the exclusively signed agreement of the Ponti heirs and the artistic director of Cerri & Associati Studio."
